_meta: A batch of tool calls an agent proposed in one turn, used to show why a harness should GATE irreversible tool calls behind confirmation while auto-running reversible ones, instead of executing everything the model proposes. tools maps each tool to whether its effect is reversible: a read or a list can be undone or simply retried harmlessly (reversible true), while deleting a file or sending an email cannot be taken back (reversible false). proposed_calls is the ordered list of calls the model asked for this turn: two reversible (list_files, read_file) and two irreversible (delete_file, send_email). A NAIVE harness executes every proposed call immediately, so the two irreversible actions run with no confirmation -- if the model was wrong (hallucinated the filename, misread the request), the file is gone and the email is sent, unrecoverably. A GATED harness classifies each call by reversibility: reversible calls run automatically (no friction on safe actions), and irreversible calls are HELD for explicit confirmation (a human approval, or a dry-run preview) before they execute -- so zero irreversible actions happen without a human in the loop, while the safe majority still flow freely. tools and proposed_calls are the fixture; every classification, what each policy executes, and the count of unconfirmed irreversible actions are computed.
